newsitem.title: USA: Northeastern US spot power extends loss on weather.
newsitem.headline: Northeastern US spot power extends loss on weather.

text.p: Bulk electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. market Tuesday continued their losses Monday on forecasts of mild temperatures in the region over the next couple of days.
"There's no demand in the Northeast," one Northeast power trader complained, adding buyers remained scarce despite the price decline. "Tomorrow (prices) will probably pick up."

Short-term weather outlook showed temperatures would average five to 10 degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the 30s-40s during the day, and teens to 30s at night. But readings would drop slightly below normal this weekend.
New York Power Authority's (NYPA) shutdown of its 965 megawatt (MW) Indian Point 3 nuclear plant was again shrugged off by the market due to lackluster demand.
The generating unit along the Hudson River in New York was taken off line Saturday to repair its feedwater heaters. NYPA expected the plant to resume operation in a week.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission costs) for Wednesday delivery in the eastern New York Power Pool (NYPP) faltered to $25.00-$26.50 a megawatt hour (MWh), down sharply from Monday's $32.00-$33.00 for delivery today.
Off-peak, non-firm power for Wednesday in eastern NYPP was slipped to $18.00-$20.00, down $2.00 from Monday.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday was valued at $21.00-$23.00, lower than Monday's $24.00-$26.00.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Wednesday dipped 50 cents to $15.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity for Wednesday delivery at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border was quoted at $30.00-$32.00, down from Monday's $32.00-$34.00.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for Wednesday at the NU border tumbled to $20.00-$22.50 from a quote of $25.00 Monday.

Swing natural gas prices continued Monday's decline on the expected mild temperatures. Spot gas values at the New York City gate edged down to $3.25-$3.50 per million British thermal units from $4.00-$4.25 Monday.
